subject: Post-demo: hosted suitability — traffic slices & endpoint map
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimble-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: hosted suitability — traffic slices & endpoint map

Hi Elena / Vikram,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — great to see the demo and hear specifics about how Nimble Retail plans to use model outputs for catalog enrichment and session-based recommendations. Quick recap and asks so we can scope a hosted pilot that proves out latency and unit economics: 

- Primary need: near-real-time product recs in search and PDP with p95 latency <= 120ms for the inference call (we captured longer upstream transformations in the call).
- Expected steady QPS: ~25 qps per active region, peak bursts up to ~250 qps for flash sales.
- Estimated token budget: ~8-12 tokens per request on average for the prompt+response.
- Data surface: most requests are pseudonymized product IDs; a small subset of requests include customer email hashes and storefront session ids.

Questions / next steps we need from you to propose a concrete hosted pilot (sandbox endpoints + rate plan):
1) Can you confirm the traffic profile CSV you mentioned (burst windows, hour-of-day distribution)? please attach the sample export you used in the demo.
2) Which endpoints do you anticipate calling separately? e.g., "search-recs", "session-augment", and a separate batch embedding route for nightly indexing? a simple endpoint map will help us size concurrency and cost.
3) Any hard requirement for VPC/Private connectivity for the pilot (or is hosted API acceptable if we commit to pseudonymization and no raw PII in requests)?

I can circulate a one-page hosted pilot proposal once we have the CSV and endpoint map — includes proposed sandbox endpoints, per-endpoint rate slices, and a short SLA summary.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimble-retail.com>

Cc: Vikram Shah <vikram@nimble-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosted suitability — traffic slices & endpoint map

Dylan — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers inline and attached is the export you asked for (nimble_traffic_sample.csv).

- Confirmed steady QPS ~25, daily peak windows: 11:00-13:00 local and 20:00-21:00 local. Last major promotion we saw sustained 120 qps for ~10 minutes with spikes toward 240 qps for a few seconds.
- Endpoint map: currently we expect three distinct inference routes:
  * /rec/search-recs (real-time, most traffic)
  * /rec/session-augment (real-time, lower qps but needs session KV)
  * /embed/index-batch (nightly bulk embeddings, run on schedule)
- VPC: for the pilot we are OK with hosted API as long as requests contain no raw PII and you can provide audit logs for requests. For full production we will likely require a Private VPC deployment, but we'd like to validate hosted first.

Attachment: nimble_traffic_sample.csv (csv)

Elena

--
Elena Ruiz
Head of ML Platform | Nimble Retail Inc.
elena@nimble-retail.com | +1 (206) 555-0114

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 13:30:05 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: hosted suitability — traffic slices & endpoint map

Internal note — forwarding Elena's traffic sample and responses. Key items to confirm before we send the hosted pilot:

- Burst handling: they expect sub-250 qps spikes for <30s and can see repeated fat-finger spikes during promos. Can hosted sandbox handle 240 qps bursts with acceptable tail latencies if we reserve capacity slices?
- Endpoint isolation: recommend we provision three sandbox endpoints mapped to their routes with per-endpoint concurrency ceilings and explicit KV prefix caching enabled for session-augment. That will reduce per-token cost and keep p95 in check.
- Audit logs: Elena agreed to proceed with hosted pilot given audit logs and pseudonymization. Need to confirm log retention length they need for compliance.

Proposed ask to Elena in next note: offer a 4-week hosted pilot with 3 sandbox endpoints and the following rate slices: baseline 25 qps sustained per region, burst cushion to 300 qps with 120s auto-throttle window. Include a short SLA summary and quickstart mapping doc. Also attach our hosted SLA outline and a sample quickstart endpoint mapping.

Thoughts? If we get a quick yes we can turn the uplift into a deal template (NR-2028-07-42).

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@nimble-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Aug 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: hosted suitability — traffic slices & endpoint map

Elena / Vikram,

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the sample traffic export — that helped a lot. Based on the profile you sent we've sketched a hosted pilot that should validate latency and cost before you commit to VPC for production. Summary and next steps below: 

Pilot proposal (4 weeks)
- Sandbox endpoints: /rec/search-recs, /rec/session-augment (with prefix KV caching enabled), /embed/index-batch (no low-latency SLO for batch).
- Rate slices: baseline sustained 25 qps per region, with an automated burst cushion up to 300 qps for short windows. Auto-throttle window: 120s. Backpressure policy: 429 + token-based retry guidance documented.
- Latency targets: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms for hosted path (we'll include network egress and transformation guidance in the quickstart).
- Data & compliance: hosted accepted for pilot as long as requests are pseudonymized; we'll provide request audit logs (30-day retention by default). If you need a longer retention or bring-your-own-KMS we can scope Private deployment options afterwards.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-sla.pdf (summary), quickstart-endpoints-mapping.md (how we'll map their routes to sandbox endpoints and suggested retry/backoff patterns).

Next steps
1) Please confirm baseline acceptance of the rate slices above or propose alternate numbers.
2) Confirm contact for onboarding (we'd like a single technical owner for setup and an ops contact for day-2 questions).
3) If you approve we'll send a short pilot agreement and provision the sandbox endpoints within 48 hours of countersignature.

If it helps, we can also run a short pre-pilot load test with a synthetic replay of the CSV to demonstrate tail latencies at 240 qps.

Best,
Dylan
